note: F14.19 (ADR-0242 Q2): the progress fields scripts/jev_harness.py reads, for a golden game with no committed route past its first stall. stage1-run.txt is the blind walk-and-whip body; it dies in the castle hall, and its own stage-set note says the stage-1 route ends in a death. Every field below was read on the pinned dump (whole-file SHA1 7A20C44F302FB2F1B7ADFFA6B619E3E1CAE7B546) through scripts/step_emu.py from the state mint-stage1.txt writes, and `verification` is the experiment scripts/test_ram_maps.py replays: each field is read at two checkpoints at least and seen to move (or hold) between them.
sources: https://datacrystal.tcrf.net/wiki/Castlevania_(NES)/RAM_map - $0028 Stage, $002A Lives, $0045 Player HP; used as a hypothesis only, each address kept because the checkpoints below reproduce it on this dump

lives.note: 4 at the stage start; 3 once Simon has died and respawned (the blind walk right dies to the hall's zombies)

hp.note: 0x40 (64) full; a zombie hit takes 8 (two of the health bar's sixteen cells)

room.note: the game's area index: 0 in the courtyard the game opens on, 1 once Simon walks through the castle door. It is the same byte navigation.json pins as the stage selector, and both values draw STAGE 01 on the status bar

camera_x.note: the camera's x in the area, scroll low byte $002E and page $002F; it restarts at 0 in a new area

abs_x.note: Simon's x in the area, low byte $0040 and page $0041. It restarts in a new area (48 at the hall's door), so a search reads it together with `room`

screen_x.note: Simon's column on the screen: 128 while the camera follows him

progress_x.note: the progress metric: abs_x restarts when an area changes (751 at the courtyard's door, 48 inside the hall), so a search steering by abs_x alone reads walking through the door as going backwards. One area is narrower than 4096 px (the hall's camera stops at 1280), so this is monotone across the door
